question: Does increasing training-set size and neural-model capacity cause coordinate-based quantum-chemistry potentials to acquire physically correct extrapolation, as measured by diatomic dissociation and a two-proton Coulomb stress test, and do the paper's experimental design and released artifacts actually support that conclusion?

key_findings.claim: On the paper's random in-distribution test splits, SchNet mean absolute error falls strongly as training data increase, but the paper does not estimate a neural scaling law.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 1 shows approximately straight descending traces on log-log axes, from roughly 7-9 to 0.3-0.5 kcal/mol on GDB-9-G4(MP2) and from roughly 18-20 to 0.4-0.7 kcal/mol on VQM24. No exponent, intercept, residual diagnostic, uncertainty interval, goodness-of-fit statistic, compute adjustment, or hypothesis test is reported, so the evidence establishes improving held-out error rather than a fitted power law.

key_findings.claim: The displayed SchNets trained on equilibrium GDB-9-G4(MP2) structures fail the neutral-H2 dissociation test, while the displayed 500,000-geometry VQM24 models form a rough well.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 2 displays full curves only for the 100,000-geometry GDB models and the 500,000-geometry VQM24 models. The former are nearly flat or inverted; the latter remain jagged and wrong at short range but approach the displayed density-functional reference around the well. The all-size panels report only discrete argmin and energy-range summaries and show no systematic scale improvement. The evidence therefore supports a coverage-sensitive difference between the two displayed training regimes, not a monotone cross-scale curve claim.

key_findings.claim: The paper's attribution of the VQM24 improvement to its 51,072 saddle points is not identified by the experiment.
key_findings.evidence: There is no VQM24 minima-only versus minima-plus-saddles ablation, matched-size resampling, targeted bond-length intervention, or mediation analysis. GDB-9-G4(MP2) and VQM24 also differ in level of theory, basis, elements, molecule size, number of geometries, stable-structure diversity, and diatomic content. The result is consistent with broader geometric coverage helping, but it cannot isolate saddle points as the cause.

anchors.section: Section 3.4, causal attribution to saddle-point structures

key_findings.claim: The VQM24 learning curve is substantially a same-molecule conformer interpolation test, even though every geometry index is disjoint.
key_findings.evidence: The released arrays exactly concatenate the official VQM24 Zenodo 15442257 DFT_all rows (784,875 local minima) and DFT_saddles rows (51,072 saddles) in source order; released labels equal -Eatomization_Ha times 627.503. Replaying the released NumPy seed-21 splitter shows exact-InChI training overlap for 482/1,000 test rows at 100,000 training samples and 760/1,000 at 500,000, or 475/992 and 752/992 unique test InChIs. A conservative grouping of the official compounds identifier strips only the prefix ^[3-5]_heavy_geometry/ and terminal /conformer_[0-9]+, leaving 301,669 parent groups; overlap remains 466/1,000 and 696/1,000 test rows, or 460/993 and 689/993 unique test parents. There are only 268,078 unique InChIs among 835,947 geometries. Thus Figure 1 does not measure molecular or chemistry OOD generalization.

key_findings.claim: The declared architecture sweep and the released experiment archive omit one of the six Cartesian SchNet configurations.
key_findings.evidence: Section 3.2.1 declares d in {3,6} crossed with w in {100,250,500}, but Figures 1 and 2 show only five traces and omit d=6,w=500. The 2.07 GB Zenodo checkpoint archive independently contains exactly five architecture directories and 75 one-run conditions: seven GDB sizes and eight VQM sizes for each of those five configurations. The largest declared configuration is not merely hidden from the legend; it is absent from the released results.

key_findings.claim: The capacity variable c=d times w is not parameter count and is not even one-to-one over the declared grid.
key_findings.evidence: For the exact PyTorch Geometric 2.6.1 SchNet used by the release with hidden width equal to filter width, the five released models have 151,301; 287,501; 847,001; 1,637,501; and 3,256,501 trainable parameters. Yet d=6,w=250 and d=3,w=500 both have c=1,500 while differing by almost a factor of two in parameters, and the omitted d=6,w=500 model would have 6,337,501. Width also changes quadratic weight matrices, so c cannot support clean parameter-scaling conclusions.

key_findings.claim: Every plotted SchNet point is a single stochastic training run, and the released seed does not make model training reproducible.
key_findings.evidence: The archive has one checkpoint pair and one loss history per condition, Figures 1 and 2 have no error bars, and the paper gives no repetitions. The public code seeds only NumPy for index selection; it never seeds PyTorch, CUDA, model initialization, or the shuffled training DataLoader. Training subsets are re-sampled rather than nested at successive data sizes, and validation subsets also change. Consequently the jagged equilibrium-distance and dissociation-energy traces cannot be separated from run and subset variance.

key_findings.claim: Four OMol25-era potentials reproduce much of the H2 curve across a six-diatomic panel, while AIMNet2 is evaluated on four supported species and overbinds H2.
key_findings.evidence: UMA-S-1.1, UMA-M-1.1, eSEN-sm-cons., and Orb-v3 track the displayed H2 reference reasonably well but show wrong wells, nonzero or divergent tails, kinks, and reversals across H2, Li2, Be2, N2, O2, and F2. AIMNet2 is shown only for H2, N2, O2, and F2, not Li2 or Be2. This is a useful low-dimensional stress test of the named model variants, although the paper supplies no scalar metric, uncertainty, checkpoint-byte identity, or overlap analysis.

key_findings.claim: The OMol25 coverage argument uses insufficient marginal summaries and is internally inconsistent about the number of elements.
key_findings.evidence: A histogram of the minimum pair distance in each structure and separate marginals over element identity and diatomic distance do not establish that each tested homonuclear species, charge, spin, and distance interval occurs in training. The 61,498 diatomics are only about 0.061% of more than 101 million structures. Figure 5's caption says 38 elements are present, while the adjacent prose says 45. No exact training overlap for the six evaluated curves is reported.

anchors.section: Figure 5 and adjacent OMol25 coverage prose

key_findings.claim: The reference-state design does not consistently match either the training labels or physical ground states.
key_findings.evidence: GDB labels use G4(MP2) and VQM24 labels use omegaB97X-D3/cc-pVDZ, whereas Figure 2 compares both against omegaB97M-V/cc-pVQZ and finite-basis CCSD(T). The paper calls all reference curves spin-restricted. Released foundation helpers default to singlets unless the caller supplies state metadata, but no curve driver or raw call log preserves the actual O2 arguments; neutral O2 has a triplet ground state and its separated fragments are open-shell. These choices leave physical ground-state matching unestablished and do not support quantitative claims of reproducing either training theory.

key_findings.claim: The released AIMNet2 code does not evaluate the claimed two-bare-proton system and therefore cannot support AIMNet2's Figure 6 curve.
key_findings.evidence: Two bare protons require total charge +2 and zero electrons. At the paper-date commit, the helper writes charge and spin only into atoms.info, but the pinned AIMNet2ASE calculator ignores those fields and retains constructor defaults charge=0 and multiplicity=1; if invoked as released, that helper would evaluate neutral singlet H2 rather than H2^2+. No released driver or raw predictions connect a particular helper call to the plotted curve. A November 2025 attempted repair introduces an unterminated string, never attaches the calculator to the atoms, and still does not set multiplicity.

key_findings.claim: Figure 6 does not establish its strongest sign, stability, or learned-Coulomb claims even for the models whose +2 charge metadata may have been passed correctly.
key_findings.evidence: The exact Born-Oppenheimer curve is 332.06371/R(angstrom) kcal/mol, but raw ML total energies carry learned elemental/reference offsets; a negative absolute energy or a roughly -500 kcal/mol tail is not evidence of binding. Each curve should be compared after subtracting its own large-R value or asymptote, or through force. The visible wells would still indicate spurious attraction for an API actually verified at charge +2, but no released driver preserves those calls and the AIMNet2 helper contradicts that state. Moreover, AIMNet2's explicit term uses learned partial charges and a short-range-damped interaction, not the nuclear ZjZl/R term of Equation 4, so its failure is not evidence that a hard-coded nuclear Coulomb law was forgotten.

key_findings.claim: The public artifacts preserve data and checkpoints but do not reproduce the paper end to end without reconstruction and code repair.
key_findings.evidence: Zenodo provides three archives containing the two training datasets and 75 checkpoint directories, and the GitHub repository pins four environment files and training/inference helpers. It omits plotting code, test-MAE evaluation, BDE normalization and minimization, PySCF reference inputs, OMol25 extraction, raw foundation predictions, and numeric figure data. The example batch script exports N_Test while the trainer requires N_TEST, and the current AIMNet2 helper has a syntax error. There are no tags, releases, tests, or exact figure-generation commands.

key_findings.claim: The experiments support a narrow warning about coordinate-only pretrained MLIPs, not a general negative conclusion about neural quantum chemistry or scaling.
key_findings.evidence: The controlled part uses one local SchNet family, one random split seed, equilibrium-heavy atomization labels, and one OOD molecule. The foundation panel is observational across architectures, objectives, datasets, charge semantics, and training budgets. Neural wavefunction methods that solve an electronic problem per system, physics-constrained MLIPs, delta-learning, active coverage, and explicitly asymptotic models answer different questions and can improve dissociation. The defensible result is that lower IID error and larger pretraining alone do not guarantee unseen physical limits.

method.core_idea: Separate in-distribution predictive scaling from physical extrapolation: train a fixed SchNet family over data-size and architecture grids, then stress the trained models and several universal MLIPs on simple potential-energy curves whose qualitative limits are known.
method.mechanism: SchNet predicts positive total atomization energy from nuclear charges and Cartesian coordinates for random geometry splits of GDB-9-G4(MP2) and VQM24. Five released depth-width configurations are trained with AdamW and validation early stopping over seven or eight data sizes. The selected checkpoints are evaluated on a neutral-H2 distance grid and summarized by the grid minimum and energy range. Separately, named UMA-S/M, eSEN-sm-cons., and Orb-v3 conservative OMol25 variants are queried for six neutral diatomics, while AIMNet2 is shown for four supported species; all five are plotted for a purported charge-+2 H2 system, with PySCF density-functional and coupled-cluster curves used as references.
assumptions: Random geometry-level test MAE is a meaningful baseline for discussing scaling even when conformers of the same molecule occur in train and test.
One 1,000-geometry test split represents each dataset over the full data-size sweep.
One stochastic training run per condition is sufficient to resolve architecture and data-size effects.
A NumPy split seed is sufficient reproducibility despite unseeded model initialization, CUDA, and DataLoader shuffling.
Independently sampled rather than nested training subsets do not materially distort the learning curve.
The product of interaction depth and hidden width is a valid proxy for SchNet capacity despite quadratic width dependence.
Omitting the d=6,w=500 condition does not change conclusions stated for the declared Cartesian grid.
A visually straight trace on log-log axes is enough to call the result a power law.
H2 is absent enough from equilibrium-heavy training to function as an OOD physics test rather than an ordinary sample-level test.
A discrete distance grid adequately estimates equilibrium distance and dissociation energy without interpolation or uncertainty.
Reference curves at different electronic-structure levels can diagnose qualitative learning from G4(MP2) and omegaB97X-D3 labels.
Spin-restricted curves are suitable for every tested diatomic, including O2 and dissociation fragments.
Differences between GDB-9-G4(MP2) and VQM24 can be attributed mainly to saddle-point or off-equilibrium coverage.
The minimum pair distance per structure is a useful proxy for training coverage of chemically bonded distance regimes.
Marginal element and distance histograms establish support for each evaluated species, charge, spin, and distance combination.
All foundation-model helpers pass charge and multiplicity with the semantics expected by their respective calculators.
A coordinate-based MLIP is defined on a zero-electron two-proton query even if that electronic state was absent from training.
Absolute energy zero points are directly comparable between each MLIP and the physical H2^2+ reference.
A learned, damped partial-charge interaction in AIMNet2 is equivalent to the nuclear-nuclear Coulomb term in the electronic Hamiltonian.
A small set of one-dimensional curves is enough to generalize from the tested models to current large-scale quantum-chemistry ML broadly.

techniques.role: Varies SchNet training geometries from 100 to 100,000 or 500,000 while retaining a fixed random test index set.
Varies interaction blocks and hidden/filter width as the paper's model-capacity intervention.
Trains a sum-readout SchNet on scaled total atomization energy.
Selects the lowest-validation-loss checkpoint with warmup and plateau-based learning-rate reduction.
Uses the smallest neutral molecule as a bond-compression and dissociation extrapolation probe.
Visually inspects repulsive walls, wells, kinks, tails, and reversals over six diatomic potential-energy curves.
Queries five 2025 pretrained interatomic potentials without task-specific fine-tuning.
Attempts to isolate a known 1/R nuclear-repulsion limit with a zero-electron two-proton system.
Summarizes minimum pair distances and OMol25 diatomic element/distance marginals as training-coverage proxies.

evaluations.setting: Five released SchNet configurations over seven GDB-9-G4(MP2) and eight VQM24 training sizes.
evaluations.metric: Mean absolute error on a fixed 1,000-geometry random test split.
evaluations.result: Held-out MAE falls approximately linearly on log-log axes and reaches sub-kcal/mol values at the largest sizes, but no scaling exponent or uncertainty is estimated and the VQM test heavily overlaps training at molecule identity level.
evaluations.baseline: A horizontal 1 kcal/mol line; there is no repeated-seed, nested-subset, grouped-split, compute-matched, or fitted-law baseline.

evaluations.setting: Neutral H2 over a bond-length grid for SchNets trained on GDB-9-G4(MP2) or VQM24.
evaluations.metric: Potential-energy-curve shape, discrete equilibrium distance, and energy range interpreted as dissociation energy.
evaluations.result: The displayed 100,000-sample GDB curves are flat or inverted, while the displayed 500,000-sample VQM curves recover a rough well but retain short-range, curvature, and smoothness defects; all-size summaries show no systematic gain.
evaluations.baseline: Spin-restricted omegaB97M-V/cc-pVQZ and finite-basis CCSD(T)/cc-pVQZ curves, which do not match both training-label theories.

evaluations.setting: UMA-S-1.1, UMA-M-1.1, OMol25 eSEN-sm-cons., and Orb-v3 conservative OMol25 on H2, Li2, Be2, N2, O2, and F2; AIMNet2 on H2, N2, O2, and F2.
evaluations.metric: Visual qualitative agreement of BDE curves over about 0.1-6 angstrom.
evaluations.result: Most models handle H2 better than the other species, but every model shows serious errors somewhere in the panel; no aggregate metric, confidence interval, or exact training-overlap analysis is supplied.
evaluations.baseline: Spin-restricted omegaB97M-V/def2-TZVPD curves; released helpers default to singlets unless state metadata is supplied, but the absent driver leaves the actual O2 model-call multiplicity unverified.

evaluations.metric: Counts of diatomic elements and bond lengths plus minimum interatomic distance over the full dataset.
evaluations.result: The paper reports 61,498 diatomics and broad distance coverage, but contradicts itself between 38 and 45 elements and does not establish pair-specific charge-spin-distance coverage.
evaluations.baseline: Marginal histograms only; no exact-neighbor, species-conditioned, or trajectory-overlap baseline.

evaluations.setting: Purported H2^2+ curve for five foundation potentials.
evaluations.result: The plotted curves have attractive wells and large offsets, but raw signs are not comparable. No released driver establishes the five actual calls, and the paper-date AIMNet2 helper would query neutral singlet H2 rather than charge +2, so the five-model artifact replication fails. The offset-normalized wells remain evidence of attraction only for calls independently verified at +2.
evaluations.baseline: Exact nuclear repulsion for two protons; a valid comparison would subtract each model's own large-R value or asymptote, or compare forces, after verifying charge +2 and multiplicity.

evaluations.setting: Official GitHub and Zenodo reproducibility artifacts.
evaluations.metric: Source-to-method correspondence, environment pins, split/checkpoint provenance, and end-to-end figure regenerability.
evaluations.result: The data and 75 single-run checkpoint conditions are preserved, but the omitted sixth architecture, unseeded training, broken batch example, invalid current AIMNet2 helper, and absent evaluation/plot/reference scripts prevent direct regeneration.
evaluations.baseline: The paper's claim that all data and code needed to reproduce the results are available.

limitations: The controlled scaling experiment covers one local SchNet architecture, two atomization datasets, one OOD molecule, and five rather than the declared six architecture configurations.
There is one stochastic run per condition, no uncertainty, and no PyTorch/CUDA/DataLoader seed.
The capacity proxy d times w is not parameter count and aliases two materially different models.
No exponent or compute-optimal frontier is fitted, so the paper tests improving learning curves rather than formal neural scaling laws.
VQM24 random geometry splits leak same-InChI conformers across train and test and cannot support molecular-OOD interpretations of Figure 1.
Training subsets are independently sampled rather than nested and validation subsets change with data size.
The causal role of saddle points is confounded and unablated.
Reference electronic-structure methods do not match both training label theories, and spin-restricted O2 is not its physical ground state.
Grid-based equilibrium and dissociation summaries have no stated interpolation, resolution sensitivity, or uncertainty.
The foundation comparison mixes architectures, objectives, data, model size, charge semantics, and domains and is not a controlled scale intervention.
OMol25 marginal histograms do not demonstrate support for the exact evaluated species and states.
A zero-electron charge-+2 system lies outside the documented support of several evaluated MLIPs, so API semantics must be validated before interpreting outputs.
The AIMNet2 paper-time helper ignores charge and the current helper is syntactically and operationally broken.
Absolute MLIP energy offsets invalidate Figure 6's wrong-sign and roughly -500 kcal/mol stability arguments unless curves are normalized.
AIMNet2's learned damped partial-charge interaction is not a hard-coded nuclear ZjZl/R term.
The release lacks raw predictions and scripts for evaluation, PySCF references, OMol25 analysis, and every figure.
failure_modes: A low random-split MAE hides molecular-identity leakage and says little about new chemical species or geometric regimes.
A local cutoff model becomes constant after graph disconnection and cannot learn a genuine long-range tail from ordinary atomization labels.
Near-equilibrium sampling underrepresents repulsive walls, bond cleavage, charge separation, and high-energy transition regions.
Marginal element and distance coverage masks absence of the exact pair, charge, spin, or environment needed at test time.
A model with the wrong charge or multiplicity answers a different electronic problem while still returning a numerically plausible energy.
Learned atomic reference offsets make raw absolute-energy signs look physically meaningful when only energy differences or forces are comparable.
A partial-charge electrostatics module is mistaken for exact nuclear repulsion and is credited with a limit it was not designed to enforce.
One random initialization or independently sampled subset creates apparent nonmonotonic scale effects.
A width-depth product ranks architectures incorrectly because parameter count and optimization difficulty grow differently with width and depth.
A discrete curve grid misses narrow minima, kinks, force discontinuities, or short-range divergence.
Cross-model comparisons attribute behavior to scale even though training data, loss, cutoff, architecture, and target states all change.
A stress test so far outside the supported state space diagnoses API extrapolation rather than whether the model learned physics within its advertised domain.
reusable_insights: Pair every IID scaling curve with deployment-relevant OOD curves; lower test loss is not a physical-validity certificate.
Group molecular geometries by parent identity before splitting whenever conformers or reaction-path frames recur.
Use nested training subsets, multiple seeds, fitted exponents, residual checks, and uncertainty when making scaling-law claims.
Report actual parameter count, FLOPs, wall time, and data size separately instead of collapsing architecture into an aliased proxy.
Treat simple potential-energy curves as unit tests with explicit repulsive-wall, equilibrium, dissociation, force-sign, smoothness, and asymptote assertions.
Condition coverage audits jointly on element pair, stoichiometry, total charge, multiplicity, distance, and environment rather than using marginals.
Verify state metadata at the calculator boundary and test it with a case whose energy changes when charge or spin changes.
Normalize each learned energy curve to its own fragment limit or evaluate forces before judging binding and sign.
Distinguish nuclear Coulomb constraints, learned partial-charge electrostatics, dispersion, and local learned energy; they enforce different limits.
A causal data-coverage claim needs a matched ablation that adds the proposed geometries while holding chemistry, theory, and sample budget fixed.
Publish numeric curve arrays, exact state inputs, reference-calculation decks, evaluation code, and plot code alongside checkpoints.
Scope conclusions to coordinate-based MLIPs; neural wavefunctions, delta-learning, active sampling, and physics-constrained models test different hypotheses.
open_questions: Do the SchNet H2 conclusions persist under nested molecule-grouped splits, at least five training seeds, and the omitted 6-by-500 model?
What exponents and irreducible errors emerge when parameter count, data, and compute are varied independently and fitted prospectively?
Does a VQM24 minima-only versus matched minima-plus-saddles experiment causally isolate off-equilibrium coverage?
Which exact OMol25 frames overlap each tested diatomic species, multiplicity, charge, and distance, and how does error vary with nearest-training distance?
What do the foundation curves look like after correct state metadata and per-model fragment normalization are verified?
Does ground-state triplet O2 change the relative model assessment compared with the released singlet-default curve?
Can hard nuclear repulsion, fragment additivity, charge conservation, and correct long-range asymptotes be imposed without reducing in-domain accuracy?
Which one-dimensional smoothness and force metrics best predict downstream reactive dynamics and simulation stability?
How much targeted path data is needed to repair each missing physical regime, and does that amount scale with chemistry rather than raw dataset size?
Can uncertainty or representation-distance diagnostics reject unsupported physical states before a simulator enters them?
Do larger models improve OOD curves once the training distribution explicitly contains the required physical support, or do architecture priors dominate?
How should a universal MLIP declare and mechanically enforce its supported elements, charges, multiplicities, electron counts, and distance domain?

competitive_landscape.title: Probing out-of-distribution generalization in machine learning for materials
competitive_landscape.difference: This same-senior-author study uses more than 700 chemistry and symmetry shifts and already shows that more data or training can improve ID error while barely helping or worsening true OOD performance. The target changes from materials-property prediction to atomistic energy curves and adds controlled SchNet capacity plus Coulomb probes.

competitive_landscape.title: MLIP Arena: Advancing Fairness and Transparency in Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials via an Open, Accessible Benchmark Platform
competitive_landscape.difference: MLIP Arena densely scans periodic-table homonuclear pair curves from short-range repulsion through dissociation and defines jumps, force flips, ranks, and tortuosity. It predates the target's first public OpenReview posting by one day; the target adds joint data/capacity scaling, OMol25 molecular models, high-level BDE comparisons, and a two-proton query.
competitive_landscape.source_version: NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks spotlight, published 2025-09-18, modified 2026-04-23

competitive_landscape.title: Global properties of the energy landscape: a testing and training arena for machine learned potentials
competitive_landscape.difference: Landscape17 evaluates complete kinetic transition networks and finds missed DFT paths plus spurious stable structures. It is a richer multidimensional PES-topology audit; the target uses simpler interpretable curves and directly separates ID data scaling from one OOD task.

competitive_landscape.title: Data efficiency and extrapolation trends in neural network interatomic potentials
competitive_landscape.difference: This work shows test errors obey scaling trends yet fail to predict OOD error and MD stability, and proposes loss entropy as a training-only diagnostic. It anticipates the target's core ID-versus-physics warning but studies NequIP/MACE landscapes rather than diatomic asymptotes.

competitive_landscape.title: Systematic softening in universal machine learning interatomic potentials
competitive_landscape.difference: M3GNet, CHGNet, and MACE-MP-0 systematically underpredict PES curvature and high-energy states because pretraining is near-equilibrium biased, and one-point fine-tuning repairs much local softening. The target changes to molecular models and controlled H2/data scaling but does not offer a repair.

competitive_landscape.title: Understanding and Mitigating Distribution Shifts For Machine Learning Force Fields
competitive_landscape.difference: This paper benchmarks multiple force-field shifts and adds test-time spectral alignment plus cheap-physics gradient updates. It has broader shift taxonomy and mitigation; the target provides a more elementary dissociation/Coulomb stress test and scale contrast.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning Smooth and Expressive Interatomic Potentials for Physical Property Prediction
competitive_landscape.difference: This work shows lower held-out error need not improve downstream physics and introduces energy-conservation screening plus the eSEN architecture. The target audits an OMol25 eSEN checkpoint far outside its usual MD evaluation rather than designing a smooth model.

competitive_landscape.title: Forces are not Enough: Benchmark and Critical Evaluation for Machine Learning Force Fields with Molecular Simulations
competitive_landscape.difference: This benchmark establishes that static energy/force errors misalign with MD observables and stability across water, molecules, peptides, and materials. The target's simpler curves are more interpretable physical unit tests but do not introduce the error-versus-deployment distinction.

competitive_landscape.title: Beyond MD17: the reactive xxMD dataset
competitive_landscape.difference: xxMD supplies reactive and nonadiabatic bond-breaking configurations that expose much larger errors than equilibrium MD17. It is a dataset remedy and benchmark; the target compares equilibrium-heavy with broader data and tests the latest foundation checkpoints.

competitive_landscape.title: Beyond potential energy surface benchmarking: a complete application of machine learning to chemical reactivity
competitive_landscape.difference: Negative design and metadynamics actively seek high-energy or unphysical combustion states and trigger ab initio labeling. The target diagnoses static coverage failures without an active correction loop.

competitive_landscape.title: MLIPAudit: A benchmarking tool for Machine Learned Interatomic Potentials
competitive_landscape.difference: MLIPAudit spans fourteen molecular and industrial tasks and discloses training overlap, with UMA-Small leading external models. The target's curve tests are narrower but isolate known qualitative limits and controlled scaling.

competitive_landscape.title: Does AI for science need another ImageNet Or totally different benchmarks? A case study of machine learning force fields
competitive_landscape.difference: This paper explicitly argues for sample-efficiency, time, and cross-dataset OOD metrics instead of IID leaderboards. The target operationalizes that warning with dissociation but omits time, uncertainty, and grouped OOD evaluation.

competitive_landscape.title: Matbench Discovery -- A framework to evaluate machine learning crystal stability predictions
competitive_landscape.difference: Matbench Discovery uses a prospective materials-stability task and exposes regression/classification mismatch near the convex hull. It concerns solid discovery rather than energy-curve physics but reinforces application-aligned evaluation.

competitive_landscape.title: Orbital-free Bond Breaking via Machine Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: A learned density functional self-consistently dissociates one-dimensional diatomics with densities and forces. It establishes ML bond breaking much earlier but is system-specific and electronic-density-based, unlike coordinate-only universal MLIPs.

competitive_landscape.title: PhysNet: A Neural Network for Predicting Energies, Forces, Dipole Moments and Partial Charges
competitive_landscape.difference: PhysNet includes explicit electrostatics and dispersion and demonstrates their importance for qualitative asymptotic PES behavior. The target tests whether much larger pretrained models acquire such behavior without task-specific enforcement.

competitive_landscape.title: Incorporating long-range physics in atomic-scale machine learning
competitive_landscape.difference: This equivariant nonlocal representation builds a Coulomb asymptote and tests charged points, dimers, and dielectric response. It is a constructive architectural answer rather than a scale audit.

competitive_landscape.title: A Fourth-Generation High-Dimensional Neural Network Potential with Accurate Electrostatics Including Non-local Charge Transfer
competitive_landscape.difference: Charge equilibration and environment-dependent electronegativities address nonlocal charge-transfer failures of local potentials. The target's proton query instead probes unsupported state semantics in off-the-shelf foundation APIs.

competitive_landscape.title: SpookyNet: Learning Force Fields with Electronic Degrees of Freedom and Nonlocal Effects
competitive_landscape.difference: SpookyNet explicitly accepts total charge and spin and combines nonlocal interaction with analytic corrections. It makes charge/multiplicity verification a necessary condition for the target's bare-proton conclusion.

competitive_landscape.title: Latent Ewald summation for machine learning of long-range interactions
competitive_landscape.difference: Latent Ewald removes unphysical charged-dimer and interface artifacts at moderate cost without relying only on local cutoffs. The target documents failures but does not compare against a purpose-built long-range model.

competitive_landscape.title: Physically-informed artificial neural networks for atomistic modeling of materials
competitive_landscape.difference: A bond-order analytical baseline plus neural correction is motivated by accurate interpolation but poor pure-ML transfer. It supplies a physics-plus-learning alternative aligned with, and predating, the target's conclusion.

competitive_landscape.title: Big Data meets Quantum Chemistry Approximations: The $Δ$-Machine Learning Approach
competitive_landscape.difference: Delta-learning corrects a cheap physical calculation instead of relearning total quantum chemistry. The target briefly recommends this older strategy but does not test it on the failed curves.

competitive_landscape.title: E(3)-Equivariant Graph Neural Networks for Data-Efficient and Accurate Interatomic Potentials
competitive_landscape.difference: NequIP obtains orders-of-magnitude data efficiency from symmetry. It challenges scale as the only route, but does not claim arbitrary extrapolation or exact asymptotes.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning Local Equivariant Representations for Large-Scale Atomistic Dynamics
competitive_landscape.difference: Allegro combines strict locality, equivariance, accuracy, and 100-million-atom execution. Its OOD demonstrations remain within sampled application structure; the target probes unseen physical limits of later universal models.

competitive_landscape.title: MACE: Higher Order Equivariant Message Passing Neural Networks for Fast and Accurate Force Fields
competitive_landscape.difference: Higher-body equivariant messages give steep learning curves and better data efficiency, showing that inductive prior changes scaling. The target studies whether larger coordinate models acquire unsupported physical behavior.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural scaling of deep chemical models
competitive_landscape.difference: This study scales chemical language models and SchNet, PaiNN, Allegro, and SpookyNet toward billion parameters and ten million structures, finding power laws for energy and force errors. It explicitly notes that force validation may retain seen species; the target operationalizes the requested unseen-species and geometry stress test.

competitive_landscape.title: Scaling Laws of Graph Neural Networks for Atomistic Materials Modeling
competitive_landscape.difference: This work scales atomistic GNNs to billion parameters and terabyte datasets on predictive losses. It supplies a much larger ID scaling study but does not test far-OOD PES limits.

competitive_landscape.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Material Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Four days before the target's arXiv posting, this paper fits data, model, and compute laws for energy-force-stress learning with Transformer and EquiformerV2 models. It complements rather than contradicts the target because its endpoints are in-distribution losses.

competitive_landscape.title: Beyond Scaling: Chemical Intuition as Emergent Ability of Universal Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
competitive_landscape.difference: E3D extracts edgewise BDE-like values from Allegro/SPICE2 and reports agreement with literature and emergent reactivity. Those latent local decompositions are not full PEC repulsive walls, forces, tails, or charged Coulomb behavior, so they do not directly refute the target's curves.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Scaling Laws Surpass Chemical Accuracy for the Many-Electron Schrödinger Equation
competitive_landscape.difference: LAVA neural wavefunctions improve energy, wavefunction properties, and N2 dissociation with model and compute scale. They optimize an explicit-electron wavefunction per system rather than a supervised coordinate-to-energy MLIP, so this directly limits the target's broad quantum-chemistry wording while leaving its MLIP result intact.

competitive_landscape.title: ANI-1: An extensible neural network potential with DFT accuracy at force field computational cost
competitive_landscape.difference: Normal-mode sampling deliberately covers distorted conformations and transfers to larger organic molecules. It is early positive evidence that targeted geometric coverage, not equilibrium count alone, controls useful transfer.

competitive_landscape.title: A Universal Graph Deep Learning Interatomic Potential for the Periodic Table
competitive_landscape.difference: M3GNet establishes periodic-table universality for solid-state relaxation and properties. Later softening and pair-curve audits delimit that domain; the target focuses molecular dissociation and charged states.

competitive_landscape.title: CHGNet: Pretrained universal neural network potential for charge-informed atomistic modeling
competitive_landscape.difference: CHGNet trains on inorganic trajectories and uses magnetic moments as electronic proxies. Charge-informed solid modeling is not equivalent to explicit electron-count and fragment asymptotes in the target's molecular proton query.

competitive_landscape.title: A foundation model for atomistic materials chemistry
competitive_landscape.difference: MACE-MP-0 demonstrates broad stable simulations across phases, reactions, interfaces, and a protein, often with optional fine-tuning. Its claims are practical and domain-conditioned rather than a guarantee of unseen diatomic asymptotes.

competitive_landscape.title: MatterSim: A Deep Learning Atomistic Model Across Elements, Temperatures and Pressures
competitive_landscape.difference: Active learning deliberately samples 0-5000 K and up to 1000 GPa and yields strong deployment results plus data-efficient fine-tuning. It shows that scale can work when deployment regimes are represented; it does not test molecular bond dissociation.

competitive_landscape.title: Orb: A Fast, Scalable Neural Network Potential
competitive_landscape.difference: Orb emphasizes diffusion pretraining, speed, and materials-workflow robustness. The target uses a later conservative OMol25 Orb-v3 checkpoint in an unadvertised far-OOD molecular regime.

competitive_landscape.title: Orb-v3: atomistic simulation at scale
competitive_landscape.difference: Orb-v3 advances the speed-memory frontier and studies conservative versus non-conservative behavior. The target specifically audits the conservative OMol25 variant on elementary curves outside its published evaluation.

competitive_landscape.title: The Open Molecules 2025 (OMol25) Dataset, Evaluations, and Models
competitive_landscape.difference: OMol25 provides more than 100 million high-level DFT structures over 83 elements with reactive, charge, spin, and solvation metadata. The target's contribution is to show that marginal breadth and thousands of diatomics do not by themselves guarantee selected curve behavior.

competitive_landscape.title: UMA: A Family of Universal Models for Atoms
competitive_landscape.difference: UMA scales mixture-of-linear-experts models to 150 million and 1.4 billion parameters over about half a billion multi-domain structures. Its reported scaling concerns broad task performance; the target audits unverified physical limits of the S and M OMol variants.

competitive_landscape.title: Foundation Models for Atomistic Simulation of Chemistry and Materials
competitive_landscape.difference: This perspective frames data and parameter scaling plus pretraining as a route to transferable and OOD-robust atomistic models. The target is an empirical qualification of that program rather than the first statement that physical support matters.

competitive_landscape.title: Extrapolation of Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials for Organic and Polymeric Systems
competitive_landscape.difference: Submitted one day before the target's arXiv version, this control study links chemical-environment convergence and neighbor-list construction to transfer across n-alkanes. It studies size extrapolation rather than physical asymptotes but reinforces coverage over raw scale.

competitive_landscape.title: Evaluating the Transferability of Machine-Learned Force Fields for Material Property Modeling
competitive_landscape.difference: The study finds solid-phase behavior is recovered only when solid configurations appear in training and proposes phase-sensitive tests. It anticipates the target's coverage conclusion in a materials simulation rather than a molecular curve setting.

competitive_landscape.title: Single-model uncertainty quantification in neural network potentials does not consistently outperform model ensembles
competitive_landscape.difference: Across interpolation and extrapolation challenges, the work finds no single uncertainty method wins and ensembles remain stronger for robustness. The target exposes unsupported curves but offers no uncertainty or refusal mechanism.

competitive_landscape.title: Scaling Laws and Symmetry, Evidence from Neural Force Fields
competitive_landscape.difference: This successor fits robust laws over data, parameters, and compute and finds better exponents for equivariant higher-order models. It supports ID scaling while reinforcing that architectural priors cannot be delegated to scale; it does not test dissociation.

competitive_landscape.title: Universally Converging Representations of Matter Across Scientific Foundation Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Across about sixty models, representations align as ID performance improves but collapse to low-information states on far-OOD structures. This gives representational support for the target's narrower empirical warning.

competitive_landscape.title: Long-range electrostatics for machine learning interatomic potentials is easier than we thought
competitive_landscape.difference: A latent Ewald-style Coulomb functional with environment-dependent charges models electrostatics without supervising ambiguous DFT partial charges. It counters any implication that explicit electrostatics cannot work; formulation and state coverage matter.

competitive_landscape.title: Symmetry-restricted energy landscapes as a benchmark for machine learned interatomic potentials
competitive_landscape.difference: Two-dimensional Wyckoff-coordinate PES slices reveal artificial minima and saddles in MACE, CHGNet, M3GNet, Orb, and SevenNet. It confirms the target's warning in crystals with richer topology but does not isolate scale.

competitive_landscape.title: From Evaluation to Design: Using Potential Energy Surface Smoothness Metrics to Guide Machine Learning Interatomic Potential Architectures
competitive_landscape.difference: BSCT standardizes stretch/compression tests, connects discontinuities and false minima to MD stability, and uses the metrics to design smoother attention. It goes beyond the target with quantitative metrics and a fix, while the target retains the controlled data/capacity and modern molecular-model panel.

competitive_landscape.title: Broken neural scaling laws in materials science
competitive_landscape.difference: This work finds dataset-size scaling breaks and parameter scaling saturates for dielectric spectra. It supports non-universality of scaling in a different materials-property task rather than atomistic PESs.

competitive_landscape.title: Bias in Universal Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials and its Effects on Fine-Tuning
competitive_landscape.difference: Parallel-trajectory fine-tuning creates constrained biased data and extrapolation failure, while periodic fine-tuning and Q-residual diagnostics improve coverage. It supplies a practical correction loop absent from the target.

competitive_landscape.title: Unprecedented robustness of physics-informed atomic energy models at and beyond room temperature
competitive_landscape.difference: Physics-informed atomic energies and a high-energy prior yield stable high-temperature simulations from about one thousand points. This system-specific positive result supports targeted priors rather than universal coordinate-only scaling.

competitive_landscape.title: Prediction and Experimental Verification of Electrolyte Solvation Structure from an OMol25-Trained Interatomic Potential
competitive_landscape.difference: UMA-OMol reproduces densities and X-ray structure factors for electrolyte solvation and beats inorganic MLIPs. It demonstrates real value inside a covered domain without contradicting elementary far-OOD failure.

competitive_landscape.title: Dyna-Mat: End-to-end benchmarking of foundation machine learning interatomic potentials in finite-temperature ensembles
competitive_landscape.difference: Across fifteen foundation MLIPs, lower force error correlates on average with observable error, yet individual low-error systems still fail qualitatively and pressure is weak without stress labels. It refines rather than overturns the target's MAE warning.

competitive_landscape.title: Fast and Accurate Foundation Models for Equivariant Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
competitive_landscape.difference: NequIP and Allegro foundation models offer favorable accuracy-speed results on discovery, thermal conductivity, and near-equilibrium tasks when data are diverse and consistent. They are positive scaling-with-priors evidence but make no far-OOD dissociation guarantee.

competitive_landscape.title: Data-Efficient Construction of Material-Specific Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials from Ab Initio Molecular Dynamics Trajectories
competitive_landscape.difference: Five universal MLIPs over seven rare-event systems need hundreds to thousands of targeted frames; scratch training can beat naive fine-tuning and low trajectory error need not preserve reaction profiles. This gives practical coverage thresholds supporting the target's narrow conclusion.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper presents evidence that model and data scaling alone do not make quantum-chemistry neural models physically generalizable, using a neutral-H2 scaling experiment and a first-principles two-proton sanity check for leading foundation potentials.
novelty_assessment.evidence: It juxtaposes strongly improving random-split MAE with failed H2 curves, evaluates four OMol25-era models on six diatomics and AIMNet2 on four supported species, and attempts a charge-+2 Coulomb-only test with all five.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The broad thesis is not novel: prior work already showed that IID energy/force scaling can coexist with wrong OOD dynamics and PESs, that equilibrium-biased universal potentials soften high-energy regions, and that path data or physical constraints repair dissociation. MLIP Arena also publicly posted a periodic-table homonuclear curve benchmark one day before the target's OpenReview disclosure. The narrow defensible novelty is the combination of a within-SchNet data-and-architecture sweep with a side-by-side audit of the specific 2025 OMol25-era molecular models. The purported two-proton probe may be conceptually distinctive, but the released artifact does not preserve the plotted calls, its AIMNet2 helper would query neutral H2, and its raw-offset/Coulomb interpretation is invalid, so it cannot carry the novelty claim as executed. Later BSCT and energy-landscape benchmarks are more systematic successors.
